ru: указывать, указать (на факт); отмечать, отметить; замечать, заметить
separable: separable — *point out a problem*, *point the problem out*, *point it out*; never ✗ *point out it*. The person you tell takes *to*: *pointed out to me that the date was wrong*
gloss: To tell someone about a fact they seem not to have noticed.
examples: She *pointed out* that the deadline had already passed.
Somebody should *point out* the mistake before this goes to print.
He is always *pointing out* other people's typos.

ru: показывать, показать (кого-л., что-л.); указывать, указать на
separable: separable — *point out the house*, *point the house out*, *point her out*; never ✗ *point out her*
gloss: To show someone which person or thing you mean.
examples: Can you *point* her *out* in the class photo?
Our guide *pointed out* the oldest building on the street.
I have *pointed* it *out* to you twice already.

ru: рыться, порыться; шарить; копаться (в чужих вещах)
separable: inseparable, and often with no object at all — *quit poking around*; when a place follows, *around* keeps it: *poking around the garage*, never ✗ *poking the garage around*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*stop poking around*), transitive (*poking around my desk*)
gloss: To look through a place in a casual way, without knowing what you will find.
examples: I *poked around* in the garage and found my old skates.
She is *poking around* online for a cheaper flight.
Do not *poke around* in my desk while I am gone.

ru: торчать; высовываться, высунуться; выглядывать, выглянуть
separable: usually no object — the thing that shows is the subject: *a sock was poking out of the bag*. With a body part it separates: *poke your head out*, *poke it out*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*a wire poked out*), transitive (*poked his head out the window*)
gloss: To stick out from inside or behind something so that part of it shows.
examples: A corner of the envelope *poked out* from under the mat.
She *pokes* her head *out* every time a car pulls up.
His toes were *poking out* of those old sneakers.

ru: быстро съедать, съесть; приканчивать, прикончить; разделываться, разделаться (с делом)
separable: separable — *polish off the pizza*, *polish the pizza off*, *polish it off*; never ✗ *polish off it*
gloss: To finish something quickly and completely, especially food or a piece of work.
examples: He *polished off* three slices before anyone else sat down.
We can *polish* the rest of it *off* in the morning.
She is already *polishing off* her second bowl.

ru: совершенствовать, усовершенствовать; подтягивать, подтянуть (навык); дорабатывать, доработать
separable: separable — *polish up your Spanish*, *polish your Spanish up*, *polish it up*; never ✗ *polish up it*
gloss: To improve a skill that has gone rusty, or a piece of work that is nearly done.
examples: I need to *polish up* my Spanish before the trip.
He *polished* the essay *up* over the weekend.
She has been *polishing up* her interview answers all week.

ru: раскошеливаться, раскошелиться; выкладывать, выложить деньги
separable: the money follows the whole verb — *pony up forty bucks*, *pony up for the pizza*; never ✗ *pony forty bucks up*. Just as often there is no object at all: *somebody has to pony up*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*we all ponied up*), transitive (*ponied up two hundred dollars*)
gloss: To hand over money you owe or would rather not pay, in informal American English.
examples: Everybody had to *pony up* twenty dollars for the gift.
He finally *ponied up* the deposit on Friday.
Nobody is *ponying up* for the repairs.
contrast: The *-y* changes in two of the forms: *pony → ponies up, ponied up*, but *ponying up* keeps the *y*.

ru: заглядывать, заглянуть (ненадолго); забегать, забежать
separable: no object — intransitive; the place takes *at* or *to* and the person you visit takes *on*: *popped in at the office*, *popped in on my parents*; never ✗ *pop the office in*
gloss: To visit somewhere for a very short time, usually without planning it.
examples: She *popped in* to say hello on her way home.
I will *pop in* after work if there is time.
He keeps *popping in* to check on the baby.
contrast: The *p* doubles: *pop → popped in, popping in*, never ✗ *poped in*.

ru: выскакивать, выскочить (ненадолго); выбегать, выбежать
separable: no object — intransitive; the errand takes *for* and the place takes *to*: *popped out for coffee*, *popping out to the bank*; never ✗ *pop the store out*
gloss: To leave for a few minutes and come straight back.
examples: I am going to *pop out* for a sandwich.
She *popped out* for ten minutes and missed the call.
He is *popping out* to the bank before it closes.

ru: появляться, появиться внезапно; выскакивать, выскочить
separable: no object — intransitive: the thing that appears is the subject. *A window popped up*, never ✗ *the site popped up an ad*
gloss: To appear suddenly, especially where you did not expect it.
examples: An ad *popped up* right in the middle of the video.
Her name *pops up* every time I search for the company.
Little coffee shops keep *popping up* all over downtown.
contrast: The *p* doubles: *popped up*, *popping up*. The noun is one word: *a pop-up*.

ru: возникать, возникнуть (неожиданно); подворачиваться, подвернуться
separable: no object — intransitive: the problem or the opening is the subject. *Something popped up at work*, never ✗ *they popped up a problem*
gloss: To come along without warning, as a problem, an extra job or a chance does.
examples: Sorry, something *popped up* at work and I have to cancel.
If a cheaper flight *pops up*, book it right away.
Openings like that do not *pop up* very often.

ru: изучать, изучить внимательно; корпеть (над); вчитываться, вчитаться
separable: inseparable — *over* never lets go of its object: *pored over the map*, *pored over it*; never ✗ *pored the map over*
gloss: To read or study something long and closely.
examples: They *pored over* the contract line by line.
She *pores over* the sports page every morning.
We spent the night *poring over* old photographs.
contrast: Spelled *pore*, not *pour* — you *pore over* a book but *pour* the coffee. The two sound exactly alike in American English.

ru: изливать, излить (душу); выкладывать, выложить (всё)
separable: separable — *pour out your feelings*, *pour your feelings out*, *pour it all out*; never ✗ *pour out it*. With *heart* the object sits in the middle: *poured her heart out*
gloss: To let all of your feelings or troubles come out at once in words.
examples: She *poured out* the whole story before I could say a word.
He *poured* his heart *out* to a stranger on the plane.
They sat up all night *pouring out* their complaints.

ru: валить, повалить (толпой); высыпать, высыпать (наружу)
separable: no object — intransitive in this sense; the place you leave takes *of*: *poured out of the arena*; never ✗ *pour the crowd out*
gloss: To come out of a place in a steady stream, as a crowd does.
examples: Fans *poured out* of the arena after the final whistle.
Students *pour out* of that building at three every day.
People were *pouring out* onto the sidewalk.

ru: поступать, поступить в большом количестве; стекаться, стечься; хлынуть
separable: no object — intransitive; a named destination takes *into*: *donations poured into the fund*; never ✗ *pour the letters in*
gloss: To arrive in very large numbers or amounts all at once.
examples: Donations *poured in* after the story aired.
Messages are still *pouring in*.
Money *pours in* every December and dries up in January.

ru: лить как из ведра; хлестать (о дожде)
separable: no object — intransitive, and the subject is *rain* or an empty *it*: *it poured down all night*; never ✗ *pour the rain down*
gloss: To rain very hard.
examples: It *poured down* all afternoon and the game was called.
Rain *pours down* here for ten minutes and then stops.
It has been *pouring down* since six this morning.

ru: включать, включить (устройство); запускать, запустить
separable: separable when there is an object — *power up the laptop*, *power the laptop up*, *power it up*; just as often there is no object: *the tablet powers up in seconds*
transitivity: both — transitive (*power up the projector*), intransitive (*it powered up on its own*)
gloss: To switch a machine on and let it start running.
examples: *Power up* the projector before everyone gets here.
He *powered* the laptop *up* and waited two full minutes.
The generator is *powering up* now.

ru: выключать, выключить (устройство); отключать, отключить
separable: separable when there is an object — *power down the server*, *power the server down*, *power it down*; often there is no object: *the system powers down at midnight*
transitivity: both — transitive (*power down the laptop*), intransitive (*the lab powers down at night*)
gloss: To switch a machine off in the proper way, rather than pulling the plug.
examples: *Power down* the machine before you unplug it.
They *powered* everything *down* ahead of the storm.
The whole system is *powering down*.

ru: осиливать, осилить; дожимать, дожать; продираться, продраться (через)
separable: inseparable — *through* keeps its object: *powered through the last chapter*, *powered through it*; never ✗ *powered the chapter through*. It also works with no object at all: *just power through*
transitivity: both — transitive (*power through the reading*), intransitive (*I will just power through*)
gloss: To keep going and finish something hard without stopping for a break.
examples: She *powered through* the last forty pages before midnight.
I am going to *power through* and finish tonight.
He is *powering through* a bad cold to get the report done.

ru: продолжать, продолжить (несмотря ни на что); не останавливаться
separable: no object — intransitive; what you continue takes *with*: *pressed on with the search*; never ✗ *press the search on*
gloss: To keep going even though it is hard or discouraging.
examples: It was getting dark, but we *pressed on*.
The team will *press on* without her.
They are *pressing on* with the renovation anyway.

ru: продолжать, продолжить начатое; настойчиво осуществлять, осуществить
separable: no object — intransitive; the plan takes *with*: *pressed ahead with the merger*; never ✗ *press the merger ahead*
gloss: To go on with a plan although people object or conditions are bad.
examples: The city *pressed ahead* with the bike lanes despite two lawsuits.
They say they will *press ahead* whatever the survey shows.
Management is *pressing ahead* with the layoffs.

ru: добиваться, добиться (настойчиво); требовать, потребовать
separable: inseparable — *for* never lets go of its object: *pressed for an answer*, *pressed for it*; never ✗ *pressed an answer for*. The person pressed goes before it: *pressed him for details*
gloss: To keep asking firmly for something until you get it.
examples: Reporters *pressed for* details and got none.
The union is *pressing for* a raise.
If they *press for* a decision tonight, say no.

ru: наживаться, нажиться (на ком-л.); эксплуатировать (доверчивых); охотиться (на)
separable: inseparable — *on* keeps its object: *prey on the elderly*, *prey on them*; never ✗ *prey the elderly on*
gloss: To take advantage of people who are weak or trusting, usually for money.
examples: These schemes *prey on* people who are desperate.
He *preyed on* elderly clients for years before anyone checked.
Scammers are *preying on* students looking for apartments.
contrast: *Prey* and *pray* sound the same but are different verbs: a hawk *preys on* mice, a person *prays* in church.

ru: распечатывать, распечатать; выводить, вывести на печать
separable: separable — *print out the form*, *print the form out*, *print it out*; never ✗ *print out it*
gloss: To produce a paper copy of something from a computer.
examples: *Print out* two copies and bring them with you.
She *printed* the boarding passes *out* at the hotel.
He is *printing out* the directions now.
contrast: *Print off* means the same and is heard in the US, though *print out* is commoner. The noun is one word: *a printout*.

ru: подпирать, подпереть; подставлять, подставить опору
separable: separable — *prop up the fence*, *prop the fence up*, *prop it up*; never ✗ *prop up it*
gloss: To keep something from falling by putting a support under it.
examples: He *propped up* the tomato plants with bamboo stakes.
She *propped* herself *up* on one elbow.
They are *propping up* the ceiling until the new beam arrives.
contrast: The *p* doubles: *prop → propped up, propping up*.

ru: поддерживать, поддержать (искусственно); держать на плаву
separable: separable — *prop up the economy*, *prop the economy up*, *prop it up*; never ✗ *prop up it*
gloss: To keep something weak going with money or support it could not survive without.
examples: Federal loans *propped up* the airline for two more years.
The whole business is *propped up* by one big client.
They cannot keep *propping* it *up* forever.

ru: совать нос (в чужие дела); лезть, влезать в личное
separable: inseparable — *into* keeps its object: *pry into her finances*, *pry into it*; never ✗ *pry her finances into*. With nothing named, the verb stands alone: *I do not mean to pry*
gloss: To try to find out about someone's private business when it is none of yours.
examples: I do not mean to *pry into* your personal life.
The article *pried into* details nobody needed to know.
She is always *prying into* what other people earn.
contrast: The *-y* changes: *pry → pries, pried*, but *prying* keeps the *y*.

ru: вытягивать, вытянуть (информацию); выпытывать, выпытать
separable: what you get sits in the middle and the person follows *out of* — *pry the truth out of him*, *pry it out of her*; never ✗ *pry out of her the truth*
gloss: To get information or money from someone who does not want to give it.
examples: I finally *pried* the story *out of* her.
You will never *pry* a straight answer *out of* that office.
He is still *prying* details *out of* the witness.

ru: настраивать, настроить (себя); подбадривать, подбодрить; заводить, завести
separable: separable, and usually reflexive — *psych yourself up*, *psych the team up*, *psych them up*; never ✗ *psych up them*
gloss: To get yourself or someone else mentally ready and eager for something hard.
examples: He *psyched* himself *up* for the interview all morning.
The coach knows how to *psych up* a nervous team.
I have been *psyching* myself *up* to call her.
contrast: Spelled with the silent *p* and no *e*: *psych → psyched up, psyching up*. On its own the adjective *psyched* means excited: *I am psyched for Friday*.

ru: сбивать, сбить с толку (психологически); выводить, вывести из равновесия; деморализовать
separable: separable — *psych out the other team*, *psych the other team out*, *psych him out*; never ✗ *psych out him*
gloss: To make an opponent lose confidence by getting inside their head.
examples: He tried to *psych* me *out* before the match even started.
Their goalie *psyched out* the whole lineup.
Do not let the crowd *psych* you *out*.

ru: складывать, сложить губы (для поцелуя); вытягивать, вытянуть губы трубочкой
separable: no object — intransitive, with the lips understood: *pucker up*. Name the lips and you are back to the plain verb: *pucker your lips*
gloss: To push your lips forward, ready to kiss someone.
examples: He closed his eyes and *puckered up*.
*Pucker up* — the camera is on us.
She is *puckering up* for the photo.

ru: раздуваться, раздуться; опухать, опухнуть; взбивать, взбить
separable: usually no object — the thing that swells is the subject: *her eye puffed up*. With an object it separates: *puff up the pillows*, *puff them up*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*his ankle puffed up*), transitive (*puff up the cushions*)
gloss: To swell up, or to make something swell.
examples: My eye *puffed up* after the bee sting.
The bread *puffs up* in the last five minutes of baking.
She was *puffing* the pillows *up* when I walked in.

ru: выпячивать, выпятить (грудь); надувать, надуть (щёки)
separable: separable — *puff out his chest*, *puff his chest out*, *puff it out*; never ✗ *puff out it*
gloss: To make your chest or cheeks swell out with air.
examples: He *puffed out* his chest and marched in.
The bird *puffs* its feathers *out* when it is cold.
She stood there *puffing out* her cheeks like a chipmunk.

ru: съезжать, съехать на обочину; останавливаться, остановиться у обочины
separable: usually no object — *just pull over here*. When the vehicle is named it separates: *pull the car over*, *pull it over*; never ✗ *pull over it*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*we pulled over*), transitive (*pull the truck over*)
gloss: To move a vehicle to the side of the road and stop.
examples: *Pull over* — I think we have a flat.
She *pulled over* to answer the phone.
He was *pulling over* when the tire blew.

ru: останавливать, остановить (машину — о полиции); тормозить, притормозить (водителя)
separable: separable, and the driver or car normally sits in the middle — *pulled me over*, *pulled the truck over*; never ✗ *pulled over me*
gloss: To signal a driver to stop at the roadside, as the police do.
examples: A trooper *pulled* us *over* just past the state line.
He has been *pulled over* twice this month.
They *pull* people *over* for that all the time.

ru: подъезжать, подъехать и остановиться; притормаживать, притормозить
separable: no object in this sense — intransitive; the place takes *at*, *to* or *outside*: *pulled up outside the school*; never ✗ *pull the curb up*
gloss: To arrive somewhere and come to a stop, as a car does.
examples: A black SUV *pulled up* outside the house.
We *pull up* at the gate and they wave us through.
He was *pulling up* just as I left.

ru: открывать, открыть (файл, страницу); выводить, вывести на экран; находить, найти
separable: separable — *pull up the file*, *pull the file up*, *pull it up*; never ✗ *pull up it*
gloss: To find something on a computer and show it on the screen.
examples: Let me *pull up* your account.
She *pulled* the photo *up* on her phone.
He is *pulling up* last year's numbers now.

ru: выходить, выйти (из соглашения); отказываться, отказаться от участия; выводить, вывести (войска)
separable: usually no object — intransitive, and what you leave takes *of*: *pulled out of the deal*. With troops or money named it separates: *pulled its troops out*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*two sponsors pulled out*), transitive (*pulled their troops out*)
gloss: To stop taking part in something you had agreed to.
examples: Two sponsors *pulled out* a week before the show.
They are threatening to *pull out* of the agreement.
The country has *pulled* most of its troops *out*.

ru: выезжать, выехать (на дорогу); трогаться, тронуться с места
separable: no object — intransitive; the road takes *into* or *onto*, and the car you cut off takes *in front of*: *pulled out in front of a bus*
gloss: To drive out of a parking space or side road into moving traffic.
examples: He *pulled out* right in front of me.
Wait for the bus to *pull out* before you cross.
She is *pulling out* of the driveway now.

ru: проворачивать, провернуть; справляться, справиться (с трудным); осуществлять, осуществить
separable: separable — *pull off a win*, *pull the deal off*, *pull it off*; never ✗ *pull off it*. The commonest shape of all is *pull it off*
gloss: To manage to do something difficult that people doubted you could do.
examples: I do not know how she *pulled* it *off*, but the party was perfect.
They *pulled off* an upset in the final seconds.
Somehow we are *pulling* it *off*.

ru: съезжать, съехать (с трассы); сворачивать, свернуть (с дороги)
separable: inseparable in this sense — the road follows the particle: *pull off the highway*, *pull off at the next exit*; never ✗ *pull the highway off*. With no road named it stands alone: *let us pull off and eat*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*we pulled off for gas*), transitive (*pulled off the interstate*)
gloss: To leave a highway, usually to stop for gas, food or a rest.
examples: Let us *pull off* at the next exit.
We *pulled off* the interstate to find a bathroom.
He was *pulling off* the road when the engine died.

ru: выкарабкиваться, выкарабкаться; выживать, выжить; справляться, справиться (с бедой)
separable: usually no object — intransitive: *the doctors think he will pull through*. When something carries the person, it splits: *her sense of humor pulled her through*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*she pulled through*), transitive (*music pulled him through*)
gloss: To survive a serious illness or get safely through a very bad time.
examples: It was touch and go, but she *pulled through*.
The doctors say he will *pull through*.
We have *pulled through* worse than this.

ru: сносить, снести (здание); разрушать, разрушить
separable: separable — *pull down the barn*, *pull the barn down*, *pull it down*; never ✗ *pull down it*
gloss: To knock a building down on purpose.
examples: They *pulled down* the old hotel last spring.
The city wants to *pull* the whole block *down*.
Crews have been *pulling down* houses on that street for a year.

ru: зарабатывать, заработать (много); получать, получить (о зарплате)
separable: the amount almost always follows the particle — *pulls down six figures*; a pronoun can sit in the middle (*pulls it down*) but that is rare
gloss: To earn a certain amount of money, especially a large one, in informal American English.
examples: She *pulls down* six figures at that firm.
He was *pulling down* more as a bartender than as a teacher.
They *pulled down* record profits last quarter.

ru: прибывать, прибыть (о поезде, машине); подъезжать, подъехать
separable: no object in this sense — intransitive; the place takes *at* or *into*: *pulled in at midnight*, *pulled into the station*
gloss: To arrive somewhere and stop, as a train, bus or car does.
examples: The bus *pulled in* twenty minutes late.
We *pull in* around six if traffic is decent.
Her car was *pulling in* just as I left.

ru: привлекать, привлечь (публику); собирать, собрать (аудиторию, деньги)
separable: separable — *pull in a crowd*, *pull the crowd in*, *pull them in*; never ✗ *pull in them*
gloss: To attract a large number of people, or bring in a large amount of money.
examples: The festival *pulls in* forty thousand people a weekend.
That campaign *pulled in* a lot of new customers.
They are *pulling in* more revenue than ever.

ru: действовать сообща; сплачиваться, сплотиться; объединять, объединить усилия
separable: no object in this sense — intransitive: *the whole town pulled together*; never ✗ *pull the town together* with this meaning
gloss: To work as one group toward the same goal, especially in a hard time.
examples: The neighborhood *pulled together* after the flood.
If everyone *pulls together*, we will finish by Friday.
They are *pulling together* the way a good team does.

ru: брать, взять себя в руки; успокаиваться, успокоиться
separable: always separable and always reflexive — the pronoun goes in the middle: *pull yourself together*, *pulled himself together*; never ✗ *pull together yourself*
transitivity: transitive — always with a reflexive object (*myself*, *yourself*, *herself*)
gloss: To get control of your emotions again after being upset.
examples: Give me a minute to *pull* myself *together*.
She *pulled* herself *together* and finished the speech.
He is still *pulling* himself *together* after the news.

ru: собирать, собрать (воедино); готовить, подготовить (быстро)
separable: separable — *pull together a proposal*, *pull the proposal together*, *pull it together*; never ✗ *pull together it*
gloss: To put something together quickly out of separate pieces.
examples: Can you *pull together* a one-page summary by noon?
She *pulled* a whole dinner *together* in half an hour.
We are *pulling together* the numbers for the board.

ru: отступать, отступить; сворачивать, свернуть (деятельность); сокращать, сократить
separable: usually no object — intransitive: *investors pulled back*, *pull back from the edge*. With troops or forces named it separates: *pulled its forces back*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*advertisers pulled back*), transitive (*pulled the troops back*)
gloss: To withdraw from something, or to do less of it than before.
examples: The company *pulled back* on hiring after the first quarter.
Advertisers are *pulling back* from the platform.
They have *pulled* their forces *back* to the border.

ru: вырываться, вырваться вперёд; выходить, выйти вперёд
separable: no object — intransitive; the rival you pass takes *of*: *pulled ahead of the incumbent*; never ✗ *pull the incumbent ahead*
gloss: To move into the lead in a race, a game or a contest.
examples: She *pulled ahead* on the last lap.
The challenger has *pulled ahead* in three straight polls.
They are *pulling ahead* by two runs.

ru: отъезжать, отъехать; трогаться, тронуться (с места)
separable: no object — intransitive; the place you leave takes *from*: *pulled away from the curb*; never ✗ *pull the bus away*
gloss: To start moving off, as a car, bus or train leaving a stop does.
examples: The bus *pulled away* just as we got to the corner.
He *pulls away* from the curb without even looking.
We watched the train *pulling away*.

ru: болеть (за кого-л.); поддерживать, поддержать; желать удачи
separable: inseparable — *for* keeps its object: *pulling for you*, *pull for the underdog*; never ✗ *pull you for*
gloss: To hope hard that someone succeeds, and to let them know it.
examples: The whole office is *pulling for* you.
We *pulled for* the underdog all season.
She *pulls for* any team from her home state.

ru: накачивать, накачать (шину, мяч)
separable: separable — *pump up the tires*, *pump the tires up*, *pump them up*; never ✗ *pump up them*
gloss: To fill something with air until it is firm.
examples: Can you *pump up* the back tire?
He *pumped* the air mattress *up* by hand.
She is *pumping up* the soccer balls for practice.

ru: подбадривать, подбодрить; заводить, завести; настраивать, настроить (на успех)
separable: separable — *pump up the crowd*, *pump the crowd up*, *pump them up*; never ✗ *pump up them*
gloss: To get someone excited and full of energy for something.
examples: The band really *pumped up* the crowd before the game.
He *pumps* himself *up* with loud music before every shift.
They are *pumping* the team *up* in the locker room.
contrast: On its own, *pumped* is an adjective meaning excited: *I am pumped for Friday*.

ru: выдавать, выдать (в большом количестве); штамповать; выпускать, выпустить массово
separable: separable — *pump out reports*, *pump the reports out*, *pump them out*; never ✗ *pump out them*
gloss: To produce something in large quantities, one after another.
examples: That studio *pumps out* four movies a year.
The factory *pumped out* masks around the clock.
He has been *pumping out* articles all month.

ru: отмечаться, отметиться (на работе при приходе); приходить, прийти на смену
separable: no object — intransitive: *punch in at seven*; never ✗ *punch the clock in* (the fixed phrase is *punch the clock*)
gloss: To record the time you arrive at work, with a card or a code.
examples: You have to *punch in* before seven.
He *punched in* at 6:58 and went straight to the floor.
She is *punching in* now.

ru: вводить, ввести (код, цифры); набирать, набрать (на клавиатуре)
separable: separable — *punch in the code*, *punch the code in*, *punch it in*; never ✗ *punch in it*
gloss: To type numbers or letters into a keypad.
examples: *Punch in* your PIN and press enter.
She *punched* the address *in* and we drove off.
He is *punching in* the confirmation number.

ru: отмечаться, отметиться (при уходе с работы); заканчивать, закончить смену
separable: no object — intransitive: *punch out at five*; never ✗ *punch the shift out*
gloss: To record the time you leave work at the end of a shift.
examples: We *punch out* at four on Fridays.
He *punched out* early and nobody noticed.
I am *punching out* in ten minutes.

ru: вырубать, вырубить (ударом); нокаутировать
separable: separable — *punch out the guy*, *punch the guy out*, *punch him out*; never ✗ *punch out him*
gloss: To hit someone hard enough to knock them down or unconscious.
examples: He *punched* the guy *out* in the parking lot.
She threatened to *punch* him *out*.
Two of them were ejected for *punching* a rival *out*.

ru: оживлять, оживить (текст, сцену); усиливать, усилить; приукрашивать, приукрасить
separable: separable — *punch up the script*, *punch the script up*, *punch it up*; never ✗ *punch up it*
gloss: To make something livelier or more striking by reworking it.
examples: They hired a writer to *punch up* the jokes.
She *punched* the opening paragraph *up* and sent it back.
He is *punching up* the color on the photos.

ru: возражать, возразить; сопротивляться; давать, дать отпор
separable: no object in this sense — intransitive, and what you resist takes *on* or *against*: *pushed back on the proposal*; never ✗ *push the proposal back* with this meaning
gloss: To argue against something instead of simply accepting it.
examples: Several people *pushed back* on the new policy.
If they ask for more, *push back*.
Parents are *pushing back* against the schedule change.
contrast: *Push the meeting back* is the other *push back*: that one means postpone. The noun is one word: *pushback*.

ru: переносить, перенести (на более поздний срок); откладывать, отложить
separable: separable — *push back the deadline*, *push the deadline back*, *push it back*; never ✗ *push back it*. The new time takes *to* or *by*: *pushed it back to Friday*
gloss: To move something to a later time or date.
examples: They *pushed back* the launch to March.
Can we *push* the meeting *back* an hour?
The deadline has been *pushed back* twice already.

ru: добиваться, добиться; настойчиво требовать, потребовать; продвигать, продвинуть
separable: inseparable — *for* keeps its object: *pushing for a recount*, *push for it*; never ✗ *push a recount for*
gloss: To argue and campaign hard to get something done.
examples: Teachers are *pushing for* smaller classes.
She *pushed for* an independent review and got one.
They have *pushed for* this change for years.

ru: двигаться дальше; продолжать, продолжить путь
separable: no object — intransitive; the next place takes *to* and the task takes *with*: *pushed on to Denver*, *push on with the repairs*
gloss: To keep going on a journey or a job instead of stopping.
examples: We could have stopped for the night, but we *pushed on*.
They will *push on* to Denver in the morning.
He is *pushing on* with the repairs alone.

ru: проталкивать, протолкнуть (закон, решение); проводить, провести (через инстанции)
separable: separable — *push through a bill*, *push the bill through*, *push it through*; never ✗ *push through it* in this sense
gloss: To force a plan, law or decision to be approved despite opposition.
examples: They *pushed* the bill *through* in a single night.
The board *pushed through* a fare increase.
She is *pushing* the permit *through* as fast as she can.

ru: превозмогать, превозмочь; преодолевать, преодолеть (боль, усталость)
separable: inseparable in this sense — *through* keeps its object: *push through the pain*, *push through it*; never ✗ *push the pain through*. It also stands alone: *just push through*
transitivity: both — transitive (*push through the pain*), intransitive (*just push through*)
gloss: To keep going through pain, tiredness or difficulty until the thing is done.
examples: He *pushed through* the last three miles on a bad ankle.
Some days you just have to *push through*.
She is *pushing through* a migraine to finish the shift.

ru: помыкать, командовать; третировать; задирать
separable: separable, and the person normally sits in the middle — *pushes his little brother around*, *do not push me around*; never ✗ *push around me*
gloss: To treat someone badly by ordering them about and bullying them.
examples: Do not let them *push* you *around*.
He *pushed* the new hires *around* until somebody complained.
She is tired of being *pushed around* at work.

ru: возиться (по хозяйству); копаться; заниматься мелкими делами
separable: inseparable — usually with no object at all (*he puttered around all morning*); when a place follows, *around* keeps it: *puttering around the garden*, never ✗ *puttering the garden around*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*just puttering around*), transitive (*puttered around the house*)
gloss: To spend time doing small unimportant jobs in a relaxed way.
examples: He *puttered around* the garage all Saturday.
She *putters around* the garden every evening.
I was *puttering around* the kitchen when the phone rang.
contrast: American English says *putter around*; British English says *potter about*.

ru: разгадывать, разгадать; докапываться, докопаться (до смысла); соображать, сообразить
separable: separable — *puzzle out the meaning*, *puzzle the meaning out*, *puzzle it out*; never ✗ *puzzle out it*
gloss: To work something out by thinking hard about it.
examples: It took us an hour to *puzzle out* the instructions.
He *puzzled* the answer *out* on the back of a napkin.
She is still *puzzling out* how they got in.

ru: ломать голову (над); размышлять (над загадкой)
separable: inseparable — *over* keeps its object: *puzzled over the note*, *puzzled over it*; never ✗ *puzzled the note over*
gloss: To think about something confusing for a long time without solving it.
examples: Historians still *puzzle over* that letter.
We *puzzled over* the bill for twenty minutes.
He sat there *puzzling over* the last clue.
